title: squalify must state, or own, how text escaping depends on the .NET runtime
lead: Documents the byte-stability guarantee: descriptor bytes are guaranteed identical only within one .NET runtime major version, because JSON string escaping comes from the runtime's encoder. Fingerprints are already runtime-stable (sq-06 projection JSON). Docs only.
findings_note: sq-02 architect finding 4: JavaScriptEncoder escapes BMP code points the runtime's Unicode tables leave unassigned, so an app hosting the library on a newer .NET can get different bytes from the same squalify version. design.md:310 covers only the CLI (tool.version bump). Owner decision needed: document the guarantee as per runtime major version, or ship an in-repo escape table.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** an in-repo escape table; any code or descriptor change.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner decision (2026-10-27), verbatim: "descriptor bytes are guaranteed only within one .NET runtime major version; document it (consumers pin the package and the runtime). No in-repo escape table. Fingerprints are already runtime-stable (sq-06 ProjectionJson)."

From the sq-26 review (P5): "when documenting the per-runtime-major guarantee, add it to the README 'Use as a library' version policy, where library consumers read it."

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `README.md`: the library version policy (or the closest section after the sq-33 split; absolute links only).
- `docs/user-guide.md`: determinism and stability guarantees.
- `docs/descriptor.md`: where determinism or byte stability is stated.
- `docs/design.md`: the determinism rules, if they claim more than this.
- Check every place that promises "byte-identical" output and make it say "within one .NET runtime major version" where it means descriptor bytes, and "across runtimes" for fingerprints.
